items.title: Âmbar Energia, da J&F, reforma usina no Amazonas para operar com gás e solar
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A Âmbar Energia, controlada pela holding J&F, investiu R$59 milhões para reconfigurar uma usina termelétrica no Amazonas para operar com duas fontes, gás natural e energia solar, anunciou a companhia nesta segunda-feira.
items.body:
A Âmbar Energia, controlada pela holding J&F, investiu R$59 milhões para reconfigurar uma usina termelétrica no Amazonas para operar com duas fontes, gás natural e energia solar, anunciou a companhia nesta segunda-feira.
A unidade localizada em Codajás, de 5,4 megawatts (MW) de capacidade, está sendo integrada a uma planta fotovoltaica com capacidade de 9,7 megawatts-pico (MWp), em projeto cuja conclusão está prevista para dezembro, disse a Âmbar.
A ideia da usina "híbrida" é que os painéis solares assumam parte da geração durante o dia, reduzindo a necessidade de queima de gás, que será utilizado principalmente para geração à noite.
Segundo a empresa de energia dos irmãos Batista, o projeto é o primeiro do Amazonas a operar com energia solar e gás para atendimento dos chamados "sistemas isolados", comunidades que não recebem energia elétrica do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) e dependem majoritariamente de geração termelétrica local.
"Codajás depende exclusivamente da energia gerada na própria cidade. Com o sol e o gás trabalhando juntos, a usina ganha uma camada extra de segurança. Isso é decisivo em um lugar onde qualquer insumo leva horas de barco para chegar", afirmou Fábio Tales Bindemann, diretor de operações da Âmbar Energia, em nota.
Pelos cálculos da empresa, a geração solar poderá evitar a emissão de cerca de 10 mil toneladas de CO₂ por ano.
A usina Codajás também deve servir de laboratório para projetos de pesquisa e desenvolvimento (P&D) da Âmbar, que está estudando iniciativas como o uso de inteligência artificial para automatizar o equilíbrio entre gás e solar ao longo do dia.

items.summary: En su conversación con el presidente ucraniano, el pontífice abordó la grave situación en Oleshky y expresó su esperanza de que se facilite el envío de alimentos y material médico, así como la evacuac ...
items.body: Bloomberg — El Papa León XIV mantuvo una conversación telefónica con el presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenski, tan solo unos días después de haber hablado con el presidente ruso Vladimir Putin mientras se recuperaba de una operación de cáncer de pulmón. Durante la conversación telefónica, el Santo Padre abordó la “grave situación” en Oleshky, en la región de Jersón, e hizo referencia a la petición de un alto el fuego humanitario que le había planteado a Putin en su conversación telefónica del viernes, según un comunicado de la Santa Sede. Ver más: Papa León dice que la tecnología debe ayudar a las personas y advierte sobre la “deshumanización” El pontífice añadió que espera que la cooperación entre ambos países permita el suministro de alimentos y material médico, así como la evacuación voluntaria y segura de la población civil, al tiempo que reafirmó el compromiso de la Santa Sede con la promoción del diálogo y la paz. -Con la colaboración de Flavia Rotondi. Oct 19 : A Siberian cave already famous for yielding the first remains of an extinct human lineage called the Denisovans, who once roamed widely in Eurasia, has now produced evidence of a previously unknown large Ice Age mammal closely related to today's yak.
Researchers said they discovered small bone fragments of the animal in Denisova Cave in the Altai Mountains of southern Siberia in Russia, and obtained DNA that showed these remains belonged to a bovine species distinct from others already known, living and extinct.
In all, the researchers studied 20 bone fragments from this species — 14 from Denisova Cave and 6 from other sites in the broader region. The oldest specimen dated to about 250,000 to 200,000 years ago, and the youngest to about 27,000 years ago.
The bones themselves were so fragmentary that their shape alone did not reveal that they belonged to a previously unknown large mammal. But the researchers were able to generate 20 ancient genomes from the bones, and these showed that this was a unique species whose evolutionary lineage diverged from the ancestors of the modern-day yak approximately 400,000 years ago.

"It is unusual, especially to recognize a large mammal species from small, unidentifiable fragments," said evolutionary geneticist Love Dalén of the Centre for Palaeogenetics, a collaboration between Stockholm University and the Swedish Museum of Natural History, senior author of the research published in the journal Current Biology.
"I'd say that this is related to the advances in the field of ancient DNA, as genetics is a powerful new layer of information applied to ancient materials," said Alexandre Gilardet, a doctoral student at the Centre for Palaeogenetics and co-lead author of the study, along with Centre for Palaeogenetics postdoctoral researcher Jonas Oppenheimer.
Genetic evidence alone is not sufficient to allow for giving a scientific name to a new species, so the researchers are calling this one "Yak X."
THE ICE AGE LANDSCAPE
Dalén said Yak X lived alongside other bovines including steppe bison and the aurochs, the extinct wild ancestor of today's domesticated cattle. It also shared the Ice Age landscape with woolly mammoths, woolly rhinoceroses, horses and large predators such as cave hyenas and brown bears, Dalén said.
"I'd expect it to have looked more like a yak than a bison, given its close relationship to modern yaks," Dalén said.
Yaks are sturdily built animals with horns, long fur and a hump at the shoulders, looking a bit like a hairy ox. The largest males can weigh as much as a ton. Wild yaks are restricted to higher elevations of the Tibetan Plateau.
The Yak X discovery deepens the understanding of the diversity of large Ice Age mammals and adds another species to the long list that disappeared at around the end of that epoch.
"Using the long, 200,000-year time span of our sampling, we can see that the species may have undergone a population decline during a period of warming around 120,000 years ago, and went extinct some time after our youngest sample, about 27,000 years ago," Oppenheimer said.
The vast Siberian expanse was a grassland ecosystem called the mammoth steppe, known as such for its largest denizens. Most of the region was left uncovered by the immense ice sheets that had blanketed large swathes of North America and Europe.
The Yak X lineage diverged from the ancestors of modern yaks around the same time as the evolutionary split that occurred between the ursine lineages that led to today's brown bears and polar bears.
THE DENISOVANS
It was in Denisova Cave in 2008 that scientists unearthed a finger bone that offered the first evidence of the existence of Denisovans, extinct cousins of Neanderthals and our own species, Homo sapiens. Since then, more remains of Denisovans have been discovered in the cave and in several far-flung parts of Asia.
Some modern populations of people, especially those in Melanesia and Papua New Guinea, carry a small percentage of DNA from Denisovans, indicating interbreeding with Homo sapiens before the Denisovans became extinct under circumstances that are not well understood.
Denisovans were hunter-gatherers who survived in many different types of environments. The Yak X species might have been among the prey that they hunted.
"It seems reasonable that Yak X was on the Denisovan menu," Dalén said.

Source: Reuters

items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that Europe has 'underestimated' the Russia's impact on the continent, saying 'Russia is on the way to destabilize the entire political order' of the region. Merz told Bloomberg's Francine Lacqua that many in Germany are not taking the threat seriously enough, warning that the Russia has larger aims than the current conflict. Merz said 'this is not only territorial gain in Ukraine. They fear democracy. They fear open societies. They fear the success of European integration.' (Source: Bloomberg)

反落して取引を終えた。銀行や鉱業株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４営業日ぶりに反落した。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．６３％安と、７営業日ぶりの反落。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は２．３３％安。銀行大手のバークレイズは３．５％下落。プライベートクレジット融資に関する流動性などのリスクを過小評価するような不適切な表示をした疑いでイングランド銀行（英中央銀行）が調査していると伝わった。

鉱業株指数は２．６５％安。銅価格の値下がりを受けて、資源大手アングロ・アメリカンは４．１％、グレンコアは３．３％、それぞれ下落した。

航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．３７％、公益事業株指数は２．１３％、それぞれ値下がりした。通期生産見通しを引き下げた石油・ガス会社セリカ・エナジーは２．０％下落した。

鉱業株指数は２．６５％安。銅価格の値下がりを受けて、資源大手アングロ・アメリカンは４．１％、グレンコアは３．３％、それぞれ下落した。

航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．３７％、公益事業株指数は２．１３％、それぞれ値下がりした。通期生産見通しを引き下げた石油・ガス会社セリカ・エナジーは２．０％下落した。

ヒーリー英財務相による初の予算案公表を来週に控える中、今週は消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）や小売売上高といった英経済指標が発表される。多くの企業決算も開示される予定となっている。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞ 

４営業日ぶりに反落して取引を終えた。２０２７年に大統領選を控えるフランスで、物価高や公共サービスの悪化に抗議するデモが拡大し、政局が混迷しつつある。財政を巡る懸念も相場の重荷となり、フランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は１．１１％下落した。このほか、総選挙を１１月に控えて政治的な不透明感が強まったスペインのＩＢＥＸ指数も１．４９％安だった。

フランスの金融機関ＢＮＰパリバ、クレディ・アグリコル、ソシエテ・ジェネラルは２．５─３．４％下落。フランスの小売大手カルフールは２．２％、ショッピングセンターなどを手がけるウニベイル・ロダムコ・ウエストフィールドは２．１％それぞれ値下がりした。

ＳＴＯＸＸユーロ圏銀行株指数は２．０７％下落。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．４３％安。

一方、テクノロジー株指数は０．７０％上昇。

今週は、ドイツのソフトウエア大手ＳＡＰ、フィンランドの通信機器大手ノキア、英銀大手のバークレイズの決算発表が予定されている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　

フランス国債利回りが上昇した。週末にフランス全土で抗議活動が繰り広げられたことを受け、巨額の財政赤字削減が同国政府にとっていかに困難かが浮き彫りとなった。

フランスでは１７日、生活費の高騰と公共サービスの質の低下に抗議するデモが一部で暴徒化し、同国で過去数十年で最大規模の暴動に発展。商業・小売連盟によると、週末に被害を受けた店舗は約３０００店に上っている。

投資家は、フランスが財政を立て直すには予算案を可決する必要があると指摘しているが、今回の抗議デモはそれがいかに難しいかを示している。来年の大統領選を控えた政治的な駆け引きが、事態をさらに複雑にする可能性もある。

ＳＭＢＣのグローバル市場ストラテジスト、ハンク・カレンティ氏は、財政赤字削減や年金改革の取り組みに言及し「抗議デモが繰り広げられた週末を経てこうした動きになったことは、改革への期待が後退していることを示している」と述べた。

フランス１０年債利回りは１３ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の４．９％と、１日としては９月下旬以来の上昇幅となる見通しとなった。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは４ｂｐ上昇の３．４５％。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は１４６ｂｐと、２週間ぶりの高水準となった。それでも、１０月序盤に付けた１６０ｂｐ近辺からは縮小している。  

イタリア１０年債利回りは１１ｂｐ上昇の４．５８％。

items.title: Why have Trump’s deals foundered?
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: The Art of the Deal” was three years from publication when 38-year-old Donald Trump suggested he could negotiate Russian arms control better than Reagan.
items.body: WASHINGTON — Trump Tower had just opened and “The Art of the Deal” was three years from publication when 38-year-old Donald Trump suggested he could negotiate Russian arms control better than Ronald Reagan. “It would take an hour-and-a-half to learn everything there is to learn about missiles,” Trump told The Washington Post in 1984. It was all about dealmaking prowess. “You either have it, or you don’t,” he said. Before there was much talk of being a personal brand, Trump had landed on his: the consummate, swashbuckling, never-lose negotiator. It was an image he cultivated in the New York tabloids and later on reality TV, repeating it so often that, to his supporters, perception became reality. Now, as he zigzags the country for Republican candidates, from Florida to Alaska, Trump is exhorting voters to again embrace him as an unqualified success in a midterm election that has become a referendum on his presidency and his record as a dealmaker. An examination of Trump’s dealmaking, both in his time in the White House and in the private sector, shows decidedly mixed results. “He’s not as good at this as he thinks he is,” said Christopher Preble, senior fellow and director of the Reimagining U.S. Grand Strategy program at the Stimson Center, an international security think tank. As president, Trump’s boasts of deals have not materialized He insisted that Iran would be defeated in mere weeks. He later brokered what he called a “great” ceasefire, though it quickly fizzled. Trump repeatedly has said Tehran is desperate to make a deal to end fighting. That also proved untrue. He promised to negotiate an end to Russia’s war in Ukraine in a day. He announced an agreement that he said meant Moscow and Kyiv would not attack each other’s energy infrastructure. That pause never happened, even as the president insisted it would hold. “I said, ‘You agreed,’” Trump said in defending his assertions. ”That’s why.” Trump promised he would use the threat of tariffs to negotiate the best trade deals ever, only to offer unilateral duties nearly the whole world over. Those import taxes have raised domestic prices and sparked trade wars with America’s close friends, including Canada. The levies brought in more than US$83 billion this year through September, much of it paid for by American consumers and still far less federal revenue than Trump suggested. Even on less consequential matters, Trump’s deals have foundered. He said he had a “guy who’s unbelievable at doing swimming pools” who could fix the Lincoln Memorial’s Reflecting Pool for a little more than US$1 million. The cost has been closer to US$20 million so far. Trump’s presidential efforts follow his business patterns The president’s public acts typically mirror a well-traveled private sector pattern. He frequently boasted about doing better in negotiations than he really had, then sought to cover expensive missteps by refusing to pay people working for him, often suing them. His biggest successes came when he had maximum leverage. “You can spin a real estate deal, as, ’Oh, you know, I got the better part of the deal because I bought it for this much and I sold it for this much,’” Preble said. “There’s a certain bit of tap dancing around those details that he just can’t do given what’s happening in the world today.” Trump’s core narrative as master dealmaker had begun to fade until “The Apprentice” debuted in 2004. Allowed to play a rich and powerful tycoon on television, Trump rebooted his dealmaker persona. That image of wealth and success helped launch his first presidential run “because people feel like, ‘Well, if he’s the president some of that success and wealth is gonna rub off on me,’” said Joel Penney, a professor at Montclair State University who studies the intersection of pop culture and politics. But even now, as his approval ratings have sunk to near-historic lows, Trump still insists he is among the best dealmakers the world has known. Tim O’Brien, author of “TrumpNation: The Art of Being The Donald,” said Trump may finally find out after Election Day on Nov. 3 “how much voters believe that he’s a competent manager and a great dealmaker.” Many of Trump’s business and presidential deals collapsed Marty Latz, a negotiation expert and author of “The Real Trump Deal: An Eye-opening Look At How He Really Negotiates,” said Trump the businessman saw every negotiation as a zero-sum game. “The reality is, he did negotiate some excellent deals, but also that he did fail spectacularly in a number of deals, and that he has never really successfully negotiated as president in a significant number of contexts,” Latz said. Trump has long been guided by the notion that he can only win. “He could be a better negotiator if his ego didn’t get in the way,” said Barbara Res, a former executive vice president in charge of construction at the Trump Organization, who wrote “Tower of Lies: What My Eighteen Years of Working with Donald Trump Reveals about Him.” “Any concession that should be made, he can’t make. Then, with the other parts of it, nothing can continue. He just has to win everything.” Some Trump deals have succeeded or still might Top officials in the Trump administration go to great lengths to amplify the idea that he is a master negotiator. “I make one of those deals every day that no normal person would make,” the president said in May, defending having the U.S. take a stake in the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern rail merger. A parade of advisers, including former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, have all labeled Trump “the dealmaker in chief.” Republican South Carolina Sen. Tim Scott posted on X that the ceasefire with Iran “once again” proved that Trump “is the Dealmaker in Chief” — before it fell apart. Trump has credited his own negotiating chops with helping to lower prescription drug prices and stimulate domestic manufacturing. The White House also pointed to a long list of trade agreements that Trump announced since last year with China, Japan and countries across Europe, Southeast Asia and elsewhere. White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said “this administration will continue advancing an America First economic agenda.” “Downplaying President Trump’s record as a dealmaker-in-chief would require overlooking the nearly 20 trade agreements he successfully negotiated and the trillions of dollars in announced manufacturing investments secured during his presidency,” Middleton said in a statement. The president’s ledger also includes successes such as his first-term Abraham Accords and a ceasefire agreement that ended fighting between Israel and Hamas in Gaza — though strikes, raids and killings have continued there ever since. Neither deal succeeded in achieving larger and lasting Middle East peace as Trump predicted they would, though. An agreement on civil nuclear cooperation with Saudi Arabia is in the early stages. An accord allowing the U.S. to help tap Venezuela’s petroleum reserves that Trump calls “probably it’s the biggest deal in the history of our country” will similarly take years to pay dividends — if it ever does. Trump as chaos agent has been a negotiating strategy O’Brien said Trump long sought to create unpredictability in negotiations, viewing them as an extension of his ego: “If he’s the one causing the chaos, he’s often the only one who can end it.” The president describes his negotiating style as following his instincts and pushing for everything he can imagine, then not stopping until he gets it. “I aim very high, and then I just keep pushing and pushing and pushing to get what I’m after,” he said in “The Art of the Deal” with ghostwriter Tony Schwartz, who later became so disillusioned that he noted that Trump did not write the book and may not have even read it. Published in November 1987, “The Art of the Deal,” nonetheless made Trump nearly as well-known for his appearances on ”Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous" as any real estate venture. “We need a leader that wrote ‘The Art of the Deal,’” Trump declared when launching his 2016 presidential run. The power of the presidency doesn’t guarantee negotiating wins Latz said Trump has changed the way he pursued deals when he was in the business world since returning to the White House in 2025, automatically assuming that the power of the presidency “translates to negotiation leverage.” And a business negotiation is far different from one involving multiple countries, Latz said, like the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict with Iran, where superior military might is not always enough. “We may have conventional power,” Latz said, “and yet we may not have power at negotiation. Donald Trump used to understand that.” In business, the stakes were markedly lower, and his showmanship was not always in public view. Res said she and others on Trump’s team would often use performative tactics to keep him happy. Before meeting with Trump, Res said she often would advise those she had already negotiated with to add a small percentage to their asking price. That way, Trump could get them to agree to a lower price and feel like he had won something. “We did that because we knew he wanted to feel that he was better than everybody,” she said. Trump’s business career was often built on lawsuits Trump also thrived in another area most successful business leaders do not — going to court constantly, either by refusing to pay those working for him and filing lawsuits, or getting sued. That was another strategic choice, Latz said, because doing so often let him reduce his own costs or to settle with his creditors for far less than he actually owed. It meant “taking advantage of a system which many of us would think is morally wrong,” Latz said. ”But it reflected an understanding of leverage.” All told, Trump was involved in 4,000-plus pieces of litigation over 40 years of business, which meant even his best deals “resulted in suing,” Latz said, ”And that’s not a coincidence.” That practice has continued right into Trump’s presidency, as lawsuits remain active against everyone from the BBC to JPMorgan Chase. Res said it was not “a matter of whether he’s right, or whether he can win. The power of being able to manipulate the legal system is terrifying.” She said Trump avoided signing “a contract that allows for arbitration” in favor of court and then, cases take so long, that “people can go bankrupt in the first year if they don’t play the game his way.” ___ Will Weissert, The Associated Press Editor’s Note: Will Weissert has covered politics for The Associated Press since 2011 and the White House since 2022.

items.title: Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil asks US Supreme Court to hear case seeking to avoid re-arrest
items.author: Nate Raymond, Jonathan Allen
items.creator: Nate Raymond, Jonathan Allen
items.summary: Columbia University graduate Mahmoud Khalil on Monday asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that opened the door for President Donald Trump's administration to re-arrest and deport the Palestinian activist.
items.body:
Columbia University graduate [USN:L1N3SG0OI TEXT:"Mahmoud Khalil"] on Monday asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that opened the door for President Donald Trump's administration to re-arrest and deport the Palestinian activist.
Khalil's lawyers asked the justices to take up his case after the Philadelphia-based 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that federal immigration law barred a lower-court judge from ordering his release from US Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody.
Khalil was among the most prominent foreign students to be arrested last year as the Trump administration pursued a campaign to detain and deport noncitizens who engaged in pro-Palestinian activism on college campuses.
His lawyers say the Supreme Court should make clear immigration law does not prevent noncitizens from pursuing cases arguing they have been detained to punish them for speech that is protected by the US Constitution's First Amendment.
"If the Trump administration can punish someone for their pro-Palestine speech, this or any future administration can punish anyone for any speech," Khalil told reporters on Monday.
If the 3rd Circuit's decision is allowed to stand, Khalil faces the prospect of arrest and deportation, after the Board of Immigration Appeals in April rejected his challenge to an immigration judge's order that he be removed to Algeria or Syria.
A lower court order barring him from being re-detained remains in place for now until the Supreme Court rules. A separate appeal of the immigration judge's order remains pending.
A spokesperson for the US Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, in a statement said the Trump administration acted within its authority in Khalil's case, and it encouraged him to self-deport.
KHALIL'S BACKGROUND AND ARREST Khalil, a prominent figure in pro-Palestinian protests against Israel's war in Gaza , is an Algerian citizen who was born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria.
Immigration agents arrested him in March 2025 in the lobby of his university residence in Manhattan despite his being a lawful permanent resident, or green-card holder. His wife and their 1-year-old son are both US citizens.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio had invoked an obscure provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act to deem Khalil removable, citing his involvement in "antisemitic protests and disruptive activities" at Columbia in 2024 that the government said fostered a hostile environment for Jewish students.
He was released from a Louisiana detention center in June 2025 after the New Jersey-based US District Judge Michael Farbiarz, an appointee of former President Joe Biden, ordered the Department of Homeland Security to release him.
In January, a 2-1 panel of the 3rd Circuit overturned Farbiarz's decision, saying that under the Immigration and Nationality Act, Khalil's claims could not be addressed through a district court and instead could be raised in an appeal of a removal order from an immigration judge.
After the full appeals court declined to reconsider the case, Khalil turned to the Supreme Court.
Federal appeals courts are split on whether district judges may hear challenges like Khalil's or whether such claims must proceed first through immigration courts, which are not part of the federal judiciary but are instead run by the US Department of Justice.
The Trump administration [USN:L1N45E0AE TEXT:"last month asked"] the Supreme Court to overturn a ruling in a similar case favoring Georgetown University scholar Badar Khan Suri, another pro-Palestinian advocate detained by ICE who was ordered released.

Oct 19 : Brentford said on Monday they were working with police to identify those responsible after a rugby ball appeared to be kicked from a nearby rooftop towards their Gtech Community Stadium during Saturday's Premier League defeat by Liverpool.
A viral video on social media showed a man kicking the ball from a nearby rooftop towards the stadium, where it appeared to bounce off the roof, while a separate clip showed staff carrying it away.
"Brentford Football Club is aware of an incident involving an item being kicked from a height towards the field of play during Saturday's match against Liverpool," the club said in a statement.
"Such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful.

Brentford lost the game 2-1 after surrendering a first-half lead and finishing with nine men.

items.title: トランプ氏、女性の健康に関する大統領令署名　ＮＩＨに新部門創設へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１９日、メラニア夫人とともに、女性の健康に焦点を当てたホワイトハウスのタスクフォース（作業部会）と国立衛生研究所（ＮＩＨ）の部門を創設する大統領令に署名した。

トランプ氏はホワイトハウスでのイベントで、タスクフォースはスージー・ワイルズ大統領首席補佐官と、ケネディ厚生長官が主導すると表明。タスクフォースは１９日に初会合を開くと明らかにした。

トランプ氏は「大統領令は、保健福祉省（ＨＨＳ）に対し、ＮＩＨ内に新たな女性の健康部門を設立するよう指示するものだ」と述べた。

ホワイトハウスのファクトシートによると、同大統領令は連邦政府に対し、女性の人生のあらゆる段階にわたって包括的に健康問題に取り組むよう指示するもので、予防、診断、治療を加速させるための研究を強化し、研究成果を臨床実践や政策に反映させることを目指す。

ＮＩＨに新設される「女性の健康部門」は、同機関の「女性の健康研究室」に取って代わるものではなく、連携して機能する。

ホワイトハウスは、今回の措置は政府の取り組みを研究の枠を超えて広げ、研究成果を女性や少女のための臨床ケアへと応用することを優先するためのものだと説明した。

items.title: 米メタ、「反トランプ」デモ主催者のインスタ一時停止巡り陳謝
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - 米メタ・プラットフォームズは、全米各地で１７日に開催されたトランプ米政権に対する抗議活動「ＮＯ　ＫＩＮＧＳ（王はいらない）」の主催者や参加者が利用していたインスタグラムのアカウントが活動中に一時停止されていたと明らかにした。メタの担当者は「心からおわびする」と陳謝した。

アカウント停止の理由について、利用が短期間に集中した際、通常の閲覧ではなく、特定の作業を自動処理する「ボット」によるものと似たアクセスが増えたためだと説明している。

１７日には数千の集会が開かれ、参加者はトランプ大統領による強硬な移民政策やイラン攻撃などを非難し、１１月３日の米中間選挙の期日前投票を呼びかけた。その際、参加者らのインスタグラムのアカウントが１時間超、利用できなくなった。

メタの広報担当アンディ・ストーン氏は交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）Ｘへの投稿で、復旧作業に時間がかかったと説明。セキュリティーシステムで、投稿やハッシュタグを読み取る人工知能（ＡＩ）ツール「クロード」の使用急増が検知され、「自動保護機能が誤ってアカウントを停止した」と説明した。

集会主催者は１９日、ＳＮＳブルースカイで「インスタグラムの停止だけでなく、抗議活動や期日前投票に関する内容がメタのプラットフォーム全体でアクセスができなくなったり、制限されたりしたとの報告を受けている」と指摘。「選挙を数週間後に控え、謝罪だけでは不十分だ。説明責任を果たすことや具体的な対策が必要だ」と訴えた。

items.title: S&P Global flags potentially hidden AI debt at hyperscalers as AI spending surges
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: S&P Global warned that hyperscalers could be carrying more AI related debt than currently visible through financing structures linked to data centres and smaller AI firms. Despite rising concerns around AI infrastructure debt, the agency saw no immediate need for rating changes, while flagging profitability and escalating investment as key risks.
items.body: S&P Global warned that the world’s biggest technology companies could be carrying more AI linked liabilities than are currently visible, as the scale of spending on data centres and AI infrastructure continues to grow, according to a Reuters report.The warning came from Mark Habib, S&P Global’s Head for Digital Infrastructure, who said there was no need to change the agency’s ratings for now. However, he pointed to complex financing arrangements that could leave hyperscalers exposed to debt linked to data centre projects or smaller AI companies without those obligations being immediately visible on their balance sheets.For live updates on US Markets, click here “It is safe to assume that there is more (debt) out there that we are not seeing,” Habib said during a roundtable in London, according to Reuters.“If it's not reported, then it's not part of the disclosure by the hyperscalers. Also, if we are not rating the transactions where this liability may accrue, then the fact of the matter is that we might not have the visibility.”AI buildout creates new financing risksThe concern comes as borrowing by AI infrastructure providers and so called neocloud companies has come under increasing stress in recent weeks. Nvidia backed CoreWeave is among the companies whose debt has faced pressure as investors assess whether the aggressive borrowing needed to fund the AI buildout can generate sufficient returns.S&P expects the six biggest US hyperscalers, Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Oracle, Meta and SpaceX, to spend more than $7 trillion on data centres and other AI related capital expenditure between 2025 and 2030.The spending spree is also expected to keep their free cash flow negative until at least next year, increasing the importance of how quickly AI investments translate into revenue and profits.Habib said S&P did not have an estimate for how much additional debt such interconnected financing structures could ultimately add to hyperscalers’ balance sheets. The agency was instead trying to take a “holistic” view of the risks, he said.Profitability remains the bigger rating testFor now, S&P’s biggest concern for hyperscaler ratings remained whether the profits expected from their massive AI investments actually materialise.S&P downgraded Oracle to BBB, the lowest rung of investment grade, in July, citing concerns over its AI spending and what it described as an “uncertain path to profitability”.Habib was also asked whether the recent selloff in bonds linked to the AI buildout suggested investors viewed the debt as riskier than current ratings imply.“For now, we don't have the view that there is a major disconnect that needs to force our ratings to change at this point,” he said, adding that S&P’s ratings were designed to take a longer term view.That stance could change if the scale of AI spending begins to look unsustainable.“And that could come from a variety of drivers,” Habib said. “Further increases in the investments (by AI firms), or a view that the revenue rate of competition is getting too intense.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

Despite rising concerns around AI infrastructure debt, the agency saw no immediate need for rating changes, while flagging profitability and escalating investment as key risks.

MUMBAI, Oct 19 : Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance said on Monday that Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity were among investors who bid in the anchor book of its record $3.2 billion Jio Platforms IPO, which two sources said drew more than $25 billion in demand.
The telecoms, cloud and AI group on Monday opened its record initial public offering to institutional investors who can bid for up to 30 per cent of the offering exclusively earmarked for them, before the issue opens for public subscription on Wednesday. 
Jio Platforms allocated shares worth over 81 billion rupees ($853.31 million) to anchor investors, a company filing showed on Monday.
State-run insurer Life Insurance Corporation, French lender BNP Paribas, JPMorgan, India's largest private-sector lender HDFC Bank were among the other institutions allotted shares in the IPO anchor book.

The bids drawn were over 30 times the quota reserved for anchor investors, a source told Reuters.
Jio upended India's telecoms market in 2016 by offering free voice calls and cheap data and soon became the country's biggest mobile operator. It now has more than 500 million subscribers and competes with Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Its listing is seen as a test of what global investors will pay for that scale and for Jio's expansion into cloud and AI.
Led by Mukesh Ambani's son Akash Ambani, Jio operates Reliance Industries' telecom and digital businesses, spanning mobile services, fixed broadband, cloud, entertainment, enterprise technology and AI offerings.
Jio's IPO follows September's listing of the National Stock Exchange of India, underscoring investor appetite for large offerings in the Indian market. It will be the first offering by Reliance since its listing of Reliance Petroleum in 2006.
Year-to-date Indian IPO proceeds rose 8.3 per cent to $12.65 billion compared with the same period last year, LSEG data shows.
A successful IPO would place Jio Platforms among the top four Indian listed companies by market capitalisation, behind its parent Reliance, its rival Bharti Airtel and the country's largest private lender HDFC Bank.
Jio plans to use up to 275 billion Indian rupees ($2.90 billion) of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm.
($1 = 94.9475 Indian rupees) 

Source: Reuters

items.title: Hamilton Lane: AI’s Biggest Returns Have Been Private
items.summary: Hamilton Lane Executive Co-Chairman Erik Hirsch says much of the wealth created by the AI boom has so far accrued in the private markets, as companies stay private longer and tap increasingly deep pools of capital. With exposure to OpenAI and Anthropic through its venture and growth relationships, Hirsch discusses how investors can access private AI companies through funds, secondaries and co-investments - and why even as some of AI’s biggest names head toward IPOs, going public is no longer the default path for most technology companies. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: 米ロッキードと「パトリオット」供給加速巡り協議＝ゼレンスキー氏
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１９日 ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１９日、ロシアの弾道ミサイル迎撃に不可欠な地対空ミサイルシステム「パトリオット」の供給を加速させる方法について、米防衛大手ロッキード・マーチンの代表者と協議したと明らかにした。

ゼレンスキー氏は「ロシアの弾道ミサイルやジェットエンジン式ドローン（無人機）に対する防衛で、ロッキード・マーチンが製造するパトリオット・システムのほか、Ｆ１６戦闘機が重要な役割を果たしている」と通信アプリ「テレグラム」に投稿。「現在、いずれの面でも容易な状況ではない。供給をどのように拡大し、増強できるか協議した」とした。

ロシアはこの日の未明にかけて、ウクライナ全土に対する広範な攻撃を実施。ゼレンスキー氏は、同盟国から事前の警告を受けていなかったと明らかにしている。

Oct 19 : Netflix said on Monday its film division head Dan Lin would leave after nearly three years at the helm, marking a second senior executive departure in less than a week amid concerns over slowing engagement.
The company said on Thursday content chief Bela Bajaria would leave after nearly a decade with the streaming platform, and would be replaced by former Disney executive Peter Rice.

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 19 : A joint Lake Placid-New York City Olympic bid for 2042 moved one step closer to reality on Monday, as members of an exploratory committee met for the first time in Manhattan with the five boroughs aiming for their first-ever Winter Games.
An enviable array of arenas bolsters the five boroughs' latest campaign for the Games while Lake Placid boasts Olympic pedigree after hosting in 1932 and 1980.
But even 16 years out, committee members are working to identify any potential obstacles that could stand in their way, after the IOC overhauled bidding rules this year under new President Kirsty Coventry.
"Transportation particularly will be one of the biggest challenges. The Milano Cortina model has shown though that they were able to work through those. They didn't have high-speed rail connecting the two, but they were able to successfully deliver the games despite that," Olympic Regional Development Authority Chair Ashley Walden told Reuters.

"So it's something that certainly will be looked at and particularly I think is going to be identified as a legacy item because it is a need for the long term."
The 2026 Milano Cortina Games have been held up as an example of a successful dispersed Olympics, with events spread out across northern Italy.
No high-speed rail connects New York City with Lake Placid, a picturesque Adirondack ski town that would become the first city to host three times if the bid is successful. Housing in New York state's "North Country" also presents a potential challenge. The 1980 Olympic village was later turned into a medium-security prison.
"This is going to be a generational opportunity," New York Governor Kathy Hochul told committee members.
"The planning now, the talk, the buzz, the excitement, the people saying, well, we're probably going to need some more hotels and restaurants and housing. And I'm going to be focused on this to just inject new energy into the North Country."
Committee members include Laura Pegula, whose family own the NFL's Buffalo Bills, and New York State Assembly member Robert Carroll.
Some are still feeling the sting from New York City's unsuccessful bid for the 2012 Summer Games, when a failed attempt at building a West Side Stadium undermined an otherwise compelling campaign. The 2012 Olympics eventually went to London.
The most recent World Cup has eased some of those bitter memories, with the final held at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium and the New York New Jersey Committee welcoming millions of tourists to the region, largely without issue.
If they are successful, Lake Placid-New York City would be the third American host for the Games in 14 years, after LA28 and Salt Lake City in 2034.
Two-time Olympic Super-G medallist Andrew Weibrecht, the Games Operations Subcommittee co-chair, told Reuters it could help spark a new generation of American winter sports talent.
"When you take the traditional venue (in Lake Placid) and pair it with a large city, I think that's a great recipe for games," Weibrecht told Reuters.

Source: Reuters

FAST

LISBON, Oct 19 : Cristiano Ronaldo was suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese FA on Monday after leaving the national team camp following a rift with coach Jorge Jesus over his role in the side.
The federation's disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of 255 euros ($285.83).
Ronaldo left Portugal's base in Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark earlier this month, having accused Jesus of twice breaking his word about his role after he was an unused substitute against Norway.
Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but left the door open for his return following Portugal's 2-1 win.

The disciplinary council's non-professional section found Ronaldo had intentionally committed an offence under Article 160(1) of the federation's disciplinary regulations. Proceedings were opened on October 9 over facts reported two days earlier.
The statement did not specify which matches or activities the suspension would cover, or whether time already served under a provisional suspension would count towards the 30-day sanction.
Ronaldo later apologised for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates, saying he remained available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident.
Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca has said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved.

items.title: Private equity firm Charlesbank bets on US law firm in back office deal
items.author: Sara Merken
items.creator: Sara Merken
items.summary: Private equity firm Charlesbank Capital Partners has invested in the back-office operations of US insurance defense firm Wood Smith Henning & Berman, the law firm said on Monday, marking the latest influx of outside capital into the traditional legal market.
items.body:
Private equity firm Charlesbank Capital Partners has invested in the back-office operations of US insurance defense firm Wood Smith Henning & Berman, the law firm said on Monday, marking the latest influx of outside capital into the traditional legal market.
Wood Smith Henning & Berman, a Los Angeles-based trial firm with more than 550 lawyers across 23 states, said it created a management services organization called WSHB Support Services that will provide non-legal operational infrastructure and support to the firm.
Capital from middle-market private equity firm Charlesbank into that unit will help the law firm expand geographically and invest in technology, artificial intelligence and data science capabilities, the firm said.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed. the Financial Times previously reported that the transaction values the law firm at about $700 million. Charlesbank and Wood Smith Henning & Berman did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the valuation.
The transaction is one of the most notable examples of investment in the legal industry through a management services organization (MSO), highlighting investors’ [USN:L6N3X712M TEXT:"growing interest"] in the sector. Lawyers, consultants and other businesses are increasingly [USN:L6N43U157 TEXT:"marketing their expertise"] in advising on such deals.
Investors and others who are not lawyers are broadly prohibited from owning direct stakes in US law firms or sharing in attorney fees. The MSO model provides a vehicle for law firms to receive outside investments without breaching those professional rules. Outside investors can own or take stakes in the law firm's non-legal, back-office operations through the MSO, which is paid through the firm's revenues without any direct sharing of fees.
Wood Smith Henning & Berman in a statement said it will remain an independent law firm with its lawyers “retaining sole authority over the practice of law and client matters." The firm said it represents insurers, self-insured corporations and institutional clients.
Charlesbank in a statement said it had deep investment experience in the professional services and insurance fields that it would bring to its partnership with the law firm.
The deal follows a growing number of publicly disclosed law firm MSO transactions this year, some involving [USN:L6N46019U TEXT:""AI-native""] law firms.
Massumi + Consoli, a private equity and M&A-focused law firm, last month announced the launch of a new MSO. Another private equity firm, Darien, Connecticut-based Uplift Investors has [USN:L6N45G11Y TEXT:"inked deals"] with six personal injury firms so far this year.
Law firms Gipson Hoffman & Pancione and Troutman Pepper Locke advised Wood Smith Henning & Berman on the deal with Charlesbank, the firm said. Weil, Gotshal & Manges, Kirkland & Ellis and Frankfurt Kurnit Klein & Selz advised Charlesbank.

items.title: El papa León insta a Zelenski a cooperar con Rusia en la ayuda a Oleshki
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: El papa León mantuvo el lunes una conversación telefónica con el presidente ucraniano Volodímir Zelenski, informó el Vaticano, e instó a Ucrania y a Rusia a cooperar para permitir la entrada de ayuda y alimentos en la localidad bloqueada de Oleshki.
items.body:
El papa León mantuvo el lunes una conversación telefónica con el presidente ucraniano Volodímir Zelenski, informó el Vaticano, e instó a Ucrania y a Rusia a cooperar para permitir la entrada de ayuda y alimentos en la localidad bloqueada de Oleshki.
Los habitantes de esta localidad ucraniana, ocupada por las fuerzas rusas desde febrero de 2022, han denunciado que la crisis alimentaria se está agravando.
La conversación la tuvieron tres días después de que León pidió al presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, que organice un alto el fuego para que la ayuda pudiera llegar a Oleshki, una petición sobre la que el Kremlin no se pronunció cuando dijo que Putin ayudaría a organizar los suministros.
León "expresó su esperanza de que la cooperación entre ambas partes permita el envío de alimentos y ayuda médica, así como la evacuación voluntaria y segura de la población civil", dijo el Vaticano en un comunicado sobre la llamada del lunes.
Zelenski, en comentarios publicados en Telegram, contó que él y el papa habían hablado sobre la situación en Oleshki, y añadió: "Estamos trabajando para ayudar a nuestra gente allí. Estamos preparando una solución".
El papa, según él, le expuso sus conversaciones con Rusia sobre la situación.
Zelenski también señaló que las conversaciones se centraron en "los retos y amenazas en materia de seguridad" y en tres casos recientes en los que Ucrania no recibió ningún aviso previo de sus socios sobre inminentes ataques con misiles rusos.
El papa, que se está recuperando de una operación de cáncer de pulmón, habló el viernes con Putin y le pidió que organizara un alto el fuego para facilitar la entrada de ayuda humanitaria en Oleshki.
El Kremlin dijo posteriormente que Putin había accedido a cooperar con el papa para organizar el envío de suministros a la localidad, pero no mencionó ningún alto el fuego.
León, que asumió el papado en mayo de 2025, se ha reunido con Zelenski en varias ocasiones.
La última vez que se vieron fue en diciembre, en la residencia papal en Castel Gandolfo, en Italia, tras lo cual Leo instó a los líderes europeos a adoptar un enfoque colectivo en las negociaciones de paz entre Rusia y Ucrania.
Durante la noche, Rusia lanzó uno de sus ataques aéreos más intensos contra Ucrania en meses, disparando 16 misiles balísticos contra Kiev y la región circundante, así como más de 200 drones por todo el país.

items.title: Pope Leo urges Zelenskiy to cooperate with Russia on aid for Oleshky
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: Pope Leo held a phone call on Monday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the Vatican said, and urged Ukraine and Russia to cooperate to let aid and food into the blockaded town of Oleshky.
items.body:
Pope Leo held a phone call on Monday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the Vatican said, and urged Ukraine and Russia to cooperate to let aid and food into the blockaded town of Oleshky.
Residents of the Ukrainian town, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:"a deepening food crisis"].
The call came three days after Leo asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to arrange a ceasefire so aid could enter Oleshky, a request the Kremlin did not address when it said Putin would help organise supplies.
Leo "expressed the hope that cooperation between both parties will allow for the delivery of food and medical aid, and for the voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population," the Vatican said in a statement about Monday's call.
Zelenskiy, in comments posted on Telegram, said he and the Pope discussed the situation in Oleshky, adding: "We are working on helping our people there. We are preparing a solution."
The pope, he said, outlined his talks with Russia on the situation.
Zelenskiy also said discussions focused on "security challenges and threats" and three recent instances in which Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners of impending Russian missile attacks.
The pope, who is [USN:L8N4650IM TEXT:"recovering"] from lung cancer surgery, spoke on Friday with Putin and [USN:L8N4621IK TEXT:"asked him"] to arrange a ceasefire to facilitate the entry of aid into Oleshky.
The Kremlin said afterwards that Putin had agreed to cooperate with the pope to organise supplies for the town, but did not mention a ceasefire.
Leo, who became pope in May 2025, has met with Zelenskiy several times.
They last saw each other in December, at the pope's residence in Castel Gandolfo in Italy, after which Leo urged European leaders to [USN:L8N3XF0JS TEXT:"take a collective approach"] in negotiating peace between Russia and Ukraine.
Russia overnight launched one of its broadest air assaults against Ukraine [USN:L1N46500P TEXT:"in months"], firing 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region and more than 200 drones across the country.

Oct 19 : Tournament host Tiger Woods was not listed in the initial player field released on Monday for the December 3 to 6 Hero World Challenge in Albany, Bahamas, but could still be added as one of the three exemption spots.
The 15-times major champion has not competed in an official event since the 2024 British Open due to a combination of injuries, surgeries and legal complications. Woods accepted a five-year suspension of his driver's license last month after reaching a deal with prosecutors in his impaired-driving case.
World number one Scottie Scheffler and defending champion Hideki Matsuyama are among the 17 players who have officially committed to the Hero World Challenge's 20-man field. Scheffler, who won back-to-back titles in 2023 and 2024, and Matsuyama are both looking to become the first three-time winner at Albany.
In total, seven of the top 10 players in the world are among those in the field, a group that in addition to Scheffler includes Cameron Young, Matt Fitzpatrick, Russell Henley, Chris Gotterup, Sam Burns and Xander Schauffele.
The rest of the field will be announced at a later date.

MILAN/MADRID, Oct 19 : The Euroleague remains open to talks with the NBA over a potential tie-up in Europe, with CEO Chus Bueno warning that competing leagues would fragment the continent's basketball market.
The continent's premier club basketball competition rejected an NBA collaboration proposal at an owners' meeting held at Italy's Lake Como on October 6. 
With the NBA pressing ahead with plans to launch a new European league in 2027, the prospect of two rival competitions emerging is increasingly coming into focus. Bueno warned of the dangers of further fragmenting the market.
"If they decide to (enter into the market), it's going to be a disaster. And they know, we know, and we don't want that," Bueno told Reuters on Monday.

"We had some conversations after Como. And the position of the owners was very clear. We will always be open to listen, and to talk with the NBA about any potential deal. But it has to make sense for us," said Bueno.
"The telephone lines are open and, if something has not worked, maybe there's something that can work in the future," he added, declining to elaborate on the terms of the NBA Europe proposal.
EXPANSION STRATEGY
The Euroleague currently consists of 13 permanent shareholder clubs but plans to approve up to eight long-term franchise licences as it expands to a 24-club competition.
Bueno said the league will announce the new teams joining the competition in mid-November as part of a multi-year growth strategy unveiled last week.
Under the expansion plan, which includes a shift to a franchise-based model, the collective value of the Euroleague's licensed clubs is projected to triple to €5.4 billion ($6.06 billion) from an estimated €1.8 billion.
The league itself is expected to rise in value to €7.98 billion from €1.4 billion, or 5.7 times its current estimated value, over the next decade.
Of the current Euroleague licence holders, only 40 per cent are sustainable, but Bueno said that would change going forward.
"I think that in five years with this expansion, we could be in a position where most, if not all, of them will be (financially) sustainable," he said. 
EUROLEAGUE UNITY
Bueno also said he viewed the prospect of Euroleague clubs leaving to join NBA Europe as unlikely, arguing that the risks involved would be too great for the teams concerned.
"I don't believe this is going to happen. I think that the teams want to be together and act together. And this is what I'm hearing and what we heard in Lake Como from all of them.
"If you are divided, you lose value, and then some third party benefits. One of the things that we don't want is more fragmentation," said Bueno, adding that "it will be bad for basketball."
The 13 shareholder clubs have all signed 10-year franchise agreements tied to the strategic expansion plan.
"If they want to leave, they have a penalty they can pay, and then the clubs can also ask for individual damages. They will lose the €80 million-plus that they have in shares.
"But if they ever want to come back, they will have to pay whatever number it is when they ask to come back," said Bueno, adding: "So I think that they have a lot to lose if they do (leave)."
($1 = 0.8912 euros)

GQEBERHA, South Africa, Oct 19 : Australia paceman Scott Boland continued to torment South Africa's batsmen with two more wickets on Monday to leave the hosts on 97 runs for five wickets at stumps on the second day of the second test at St George's Park.
Boland finished the rain-affected day with figures of 4-31 to put Australia in a strong position with South Africa to resume on Tuesday with captain Temba Bavuma 41 not out and Wiaan Mulder unbeaten with two runs.
Play got underway at 3:45 p.m. local time (1345 GMT) with 30.4 overs bowled after heavy rain in the morning threatened to wash out Monday's play.
Boland, who took two wickets in the one hour of play possible on Sunday, added a third in the third over of the second day's play, inducing an edge from debutant opener Marques Ackerman, who was dismissed for six.

Matthew Breetzke, brought into the home line-up after the 214-run defeat in the first test in Durban last week, then departed for four runs after he was also caught behind by wicketkeeper Alex Carey, playing away from his body to Mitchell Starc's left-arm delivery.
South Africa were in a precarious position at 40-4 but Bavuma led a fightback with Ryan Rickelton as they put on 52 runs for the fifth wicket.
Rickelton was dropped on 26 by leg slip Marnus Labuschagne off captain Pat Cummins in what looked a regulation chance, but he only added five more runs before a brilliant one-handed catch by Matt Renshaw at first slip gave Boland a fourth wicket.
Bavuma provided some home hope with a resolute innings in spite of the relentless pressure from the Australian attack, which had to do without Josh Hazlewood, who took a career-best 6-49 in the first test but was absent with an upset stomach.
No more rain is forecast for the rest of the test as Australia look to wrap up the three-match series. Extra time is to be added to all three sessions on Tuesday.

NEW YORK, Oct 19 : IT services company DXC Technology is in advanced talks to sell its insurance software and services division to private investment firm Eldridge Industries for about $2.4 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
Eldridge is discussing combining the business with Zinnia, its insurance technology platform that provides software and digital infrastructure to life insurance and annuity providers, the sources said.
An agreement could be reached in the coming weeks, although there is no certainty a deal will be finalized, the people said, requesting anonymity because the discussions are confidential.
DXC Technology, Eldridge and Zinnia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The transaction would mark a significant divestiture for DXC as the information technology services provider seeks to streamline its portfolio after several years of declining revenue. 
The sale would allow DXC to exit a business that provides technology and outsourcing services to insurers globally, helping the IT services provider streamline its operations after several years of declining revenue. Its insurance division offers policy administration systems and other software and business process services to insurers across life, wealth, property and casualty markets. 
For Eldridge, a transaction would combine Zinnia's life and annuity technology platform with DXC Technology's insurance software and business-process services operations, creating a scaled provider of software, administration and servicing technology for insurers.

[カイロ １９日 ロイター] - イスラエルは１９日、パレスチナ自治区ガザへの商業物資の搬入を再開すると発表した。援助に依存するガザへの食料など生活必需品の重要な供給ルートが復活する。物資搬入は、パレスチナのイスラム組織ハマスと商人の間の課税を巡る対立で数日間停止していた。

ガザでの人道問題を管轄するイスラエル軍機関「ＣＯＧＡＴ」は、ハマス当局がトラック１台当たり１万シェケル（３２２５ドル）の支払い要求を取り下げたと商人側が報告したことを受け、再開を決定したと説明した。

ＣＯＧＡＴは「調整の再開は、停戦合意の人道的条項を順守するというイスラエルの約束に沿って実施される」と表明した。商人側の説明は独自には確認できていないとした上で、搬入は段階的に再開し、冬を前に生活必需品が優先されるとした。

支払いが銀行振込を通じてのみ行われ、記録に残る形で授受されるよう監視を強化する。ハマスに支払いを行ったことが判明した商人はシステムから排除されるという。

ハマスは、１万シェケルの費用は戦禍で荒廃した地域で困窮者を支援する「基金」への裕福なガザ住民による任意の拠出だと説明している。

FAST

LONDON, Oct 19 : S&P Global estimates the world's biggest tech firms are likely to have more AI-linked liabilities than currently known, although its top analyst for the sector sees no need to change any ratings at present.
Debt issued by AI infrastructure providers and so-called 'neocloud' firms such as Nvidia-backed CoreWeave has sunk to increasingly stressed levels in recent weeks amid concerns about the aggressive scale of their borrowing.
S&P's Global Head for Digital Infrastructure Mark Habib said the biggest risk to hyperscalers' ratings remained whether expected profits fail to materialise.
But he also highlighted so-called 'interconnected financing structures', where hyperscalers effectively guarantee huge data centre builds, or smaller AI companies.

"It is safe to assume that there is more (debt) out there that we are not seeing," Habib said during a roundtable in London.
"If it's not reported, then it's not part of the disclosure by the hyperscalers. Also, if we are not rating the transactions where this liability may accrue, then the fact of the matter is that we might not have the visibility."
S&P expects the top six US hyperscalers — Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Oracle, Meta, and SpaceX — to spend more than $7 trillion on data centers and other AI-related capex between 2025 and 2030, and have negative free cash flow until at least next year.
Habib said there wasn't an estimate of how much additional debt the circular financing might add to firms' balance sheets, although he said S&P was trying to take a "holistic" view overall.
Back in July, it downgraded Oracle to BBB-, the lowest rung of 'investment grade', on concerns about its AI spending and what it called "an uncertain path to profitability".
Habib was also asked whether the recent market selloff of bonds linked to the aggressive AI buildout was a sign that investors see them as riskier than ratings indicate.
"For now, we don't have the view that there is a major disconnect that needs to force our ratings to change at this point," he said, saying S&P's scores were designed to take a longer-term view.
He said what could change that view was if it became clear the amount of money being spent was no longer sustainable.
"And that could come from a variety of drivers," Habib said. "Further increases in the investments (by AI firms), or a view that the revenue rate of competition is getting too intense."

Source: Reuters

Unilever (ULVR.L) said on Monday it has agreed to sell Welly Health PBC to private-equity firm Forward Consumer Partners, but did not disclose financial terms of the sale.
The consumer products giant had acquired a majority stake in the US brand, known for its colorful adhesive bandages, in 2021 from Welly co-founder Eric Ryan for an undisclosed price.
The deal, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to customary closing conditions
Separately, Forward Consumer Partners announced that Ryan will return to the business as a strategic advisor and a member of the board
Unilever, the maker of Knorr stock cubes and Hellmann's mayonnaise, has been shifting towards beauty and well-being brands under CEO Fernando Fernandez
Forward said the acquisition of Welly would mark its first investment in the consumer health sector

items.title: Brazil detects Newcastle disease at turkey farm, raising export concerns
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Brazil has detected a case of Newcastle disease at a turkey farm in the southern state of Santa Catarina, Agriculture Minister Andre de Paula said on Monday, raising concerns about potential disruptions to poultry shipments from the world's largest chicken meat exporter.
items.body:
Brazil has detected a case of Newcastle disease at a turkey farm in the southern state of Santa Catarina, Agriculture Minister Andre de Paula said on Monday, raising concerns about potential disruptions to poultry shipments from the world's largest chicken meat exporter.
China, one of Brazil's largest markets for chicken meat, halted imports from Rio Grande do Sul after a Newcastle disease case was confirmed at a commercial farm in the state in 2024. The ban was [USN:L1N3YL0U4 TEXT:"lifted earlier this year"].
Newcastle is a highly contagious and viral disease affecting birds, like avian flu
Brazilian officials said sanitary measures have been put in place and are expected to affect 133 farms in the region, adding all relevant information will be shared with the country's main trading partners
Brazil's Acting Secretary for Agricultural Trade, Rafael Requiao, said it was too early to provide any concrete information on possible import suspensions
Meat lobby group ABPA told Reuters that Brazil's trade protocol with China provides for the suspension of poultry exports following a Newcastle disease outbreak
The protocol, ABPA said, triggers an "auto-embargo" before Chinese authorities decide whether restrictions should apply to the entire state or to a limited area around the affected farm
Analysts at Citi said that Santa Catarina accounts for around 15% of Brazilian poultry production, making the scope of potential restrictions particularly relevant

items.title: Brasil registra foco de Doença de Newcastle em perus em Santa Catarina
items.author: Victor Borges, Roberto Samora
items.creator: Victor Borges, Roberto Samora
items.summary: O Ministério da Agricultura registrou um foco de Doença de Newcastle em uma criação de perus em Santa Catarina, disse nesta segunda-feira o ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, levantando preocupações sobre potenciais interrupções nas exportações de carne frango do maior exportador global do produto.
items.body:
O Ministério da Agricultura registrou um foco de Doença de Newcastle em uma criação de perus em Santa Catarina, disse nesta segunda-feira o ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, levantando preocupações sobre potenciais interrupções nas exportações de carne frango do maior exportador global do produto.
A China, um dos principais destinos das exportações brasileiras de carne de frango, impôs em 2024 um embargo ao produto do Rio Grande do Sul após a confirmação de um caso de Doença de Newcastle em uma granja comercial no Estado. Essa situação só foi revertida no início deste ano.
Outros países também chegaram a banir provisoriamente o produto brasileiro naquela oportunidade.
Nesta segunda-feira, autoridades disseram que o ministério está informando parceiros comerciais sobre o caso da doença viral altamente contagiosa para aves, que não causa problemas para a saúde humana.
Autoridades acrescentaram que o ministério ainda não recebeu qualquer informação sobre suspensão das exportações brasileiras por conta do foco em perus, em um estabelecimento de avicultura comercial de corte no município de Nova Itaberaba (SC).
"Ainda não temos nada objetivo a informar (sobre suspensão de exportações)", afirmou o secretário-substituto de Comércio e Relações Internacionais do ministério, Rafael Requião.
Ele disse ainda que o Brasil está analisando os protocolos para identificar quais medidas serão tomadas para um eventual "autoembargo" de exportações.
"Não queremos antecipar a reação de parceiros, as discussões com a China começam agora", disse Requião.
Um acordo assinado com a China prevê que as exportações de carnes de aves brasileiras sejam [USN:L1N4650TK TEXT:"suspensas"] no caso da ocorrência de Doença de Newcastle, como a confirmada em uma granja de perus em Santa Catarina no domingo, disse o presidente da Associação Brasileira de Proteína Animal (ABPA), Ricardo Santin, à Reuters.
A China aparece como o maior mercado importador de carne de frango do Brasil neste ano --os chineses responderam por cerca de 10% das vendas totais do Brasil de janeiro a setembro, importando 420 mil toneladas, segundo dados do governo brasileiro.
A partir do "autoembargo", a China costuma definir como fica o embargo, se restrito apenas à região ou ao Estado atingido pelo foco da doença, explicou Santin.
Requião, do Ministério da Agricultura, disse ainda que o governo tem trabalhado com protocolos sanitários que permitem a "regionalização" do problema, o que evitaria embargos mais abrangentes sobre a carne brasileira.
As medidas de controle, contenção e erradicação do foco serão executadas conforme as diretrizes do Plano de Contingência para Influenza Aviária e Doença de Newcastle, disse o ministério.
O estabelecimento Nova Itaberaba foi interditado pelo Serviço Veterinário Oficial, com suspensão da movimentação de aves.
Já o secretário de Defesa Agropecuária substituto, Allan Alvarenga, afirmou que a doença não representa riscos à população. Ele acrescentou que a Organização Mundial de Saúde Animal foi notificada do caso no domingo.
Apesar da necessidade de adoção de "medidas sanitárias para controlar a ocorrência, o consumo de produtos avícolas submetidos à inspeção oficial permanece seguro, sem contraindicações", ressaltou o ministério, em nota.
Associações de produtores, como ABPA, ACAV e Sindicarne, destacaram em nota que a ocorrência de Doença de Newcastle não apresentou "manifestação clínica". Ou seja, houve a detecção do vírus, mas não da doença nos animais confinados.

items.title: Eagles quarterback Hurts set to miss rest of season due to blood clots
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent said on Monday, and media reports said the former Super Bowl MVP was expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season.
items.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent said on Monday, and media reports said the former Super Bowl MVP was expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season.
Hurts is clinically stable and his treatment should only involve blood thinners, which will rule him out of contact activities, the Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn said in a statement.
The 28-year-old was initially diagnosed with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis after an ultrasound in London before Philadelphia's 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which Hurts played in.
The current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. A bilateral pulmonary embolism is where a blood clot travels from a deep vein in the body, often the leg, and blocks an artery in both lungs.
"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners," the statement said, adding no long-term effects are expected.
According to an ESPN report, Hurts was in the hospital in London until 4 a.m. on the day of the game and did not sleep the night before the contest as a health precaution.
Speaking at a press conference on Monday, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said that the team care deeply about their players and that he trusts the team's medical staff.
"I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them," Sirianni said.
"We get medical information from our guys, and we always put the players' health first and foremost in every situation. And, you know, that's where we were there."
The Eagles said in a statement on Thursday that their medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the ultrasound results and concluded that "activity and mobility were important" and that Hurts could safely play in the game against the Jaguars, adding that he "played without limitation".
Hurts guided the Eagles to the Super Bowl title in February 2025, throwing for two touchdowns and running in another against the Kansas City Chiefs to earn the game's Most Valuable Player trophy.

items.title: Canadian firms' outlooks dimmed after trade talks collapse, BoC survey finds
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Promit Mukherjee and David Ljunggren
items.body:
By Promit Mukherjee and David Ljunggren
OTTAWA, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Canadian firms reported their outlooks had deteriorated after the collapse of trade talks with the United States but sentiments remained considerably stronger than at the peak of tensions last year, the Bank of Canada said on Monday.
A survey of around 340 business leaders in September showed that since the talks broke down on August 21, new US tariffs and Canadian counter tariffs had weighed on their outlooks.
The bank said this suggested "a moderation rather than a fundamental shift in firms' outlooks".
A separate Business Outlook Survey for the third quarter, which was largely carried out before the talks collapsed, showed overall sentiment had improved.
But both surveys pointed to higher inflation expectations amid increase input costs and elevated selling prices due to trade tensions and the Middle East crisis.
The studies help the BoC decide the trajectory of inflation and feed into its decision for the monetary policy.
Money markets are pricing in a hold in interest rates by the BoC on October 28, but see a 25 basis point rise in December.
Governor Tiff Macklem says while headline inflation has risen, this is primarily due by higher energy costs and there are so far no signs of a spillover into other components.
But he also says he is ready to hike rates if higher prices show signs of feeding into the broader economy.
The leaders' survey reported weaker export sales, the BoC said, adding that the improving sentiment at the beginning of the third quarter had partially reversed.
"Nevertheless, sentiment and expectations remain considerably stronger than at the height of trade tensions in 2025," it added.
In the Business Outlook Survey, the central bank said while there were some improvements in demand, firms' hiring intentions remained soft, but most firms intend to retain existing employees. Expectations for wage growth are largely unchanged, the survey noted.
The business outlook indicator, a metric of prospects under current economic conditions, edged up to -0.33 in the third quarter from -0.38 in the prior three months.
A separate survey by the central bank on consumer expectations showed that more than 50% of consumers surveyed expect a recession over the next 12 months and expectations for five-year inflation had also risen.
((Reuters Ottawa bureau))

AMSTERDAM, Oct 19 : Retailer Ahold Delhaize reported a cybersecurity incident to Dutch police on Monday after it detected suspicious activity in its infrastructure, the company said, adding it took some systems offline as a precaution earlier this month.
Although only reported to the police on Monday, the incident coincided with a cyberattack in France that caused refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of stores to heat up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, sparking fires and spoiling food.
The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre said there was no reason to believe the incident in the Netherlands was directly linked to any cyberattacks in other countries.
Delhaize said its investigations found the suspicious activity had resulted from the "malicious actions of others", without specifying who might be responsible.

"Taking systems offline to help protect them was a precautionary measure that affected most of our brands across Europe and the United States. The investigation to date confirms this was the right decision", President and CEO Frans Muller said.
NO ONLINE ORDERS BEFORE THURSDAY
Earlier on Monday, Ahold Delhaize's Albert Heijn, the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain, said it would not resume online deliveries before Thursday at the earliest, extending to at least 11 days an outage caused by the cybersecurity incident.
Online accounts for about 10 per cent of Albert Heijn sales.
While Albert Heijn's website was back online on Monday, the websites of Ahold Delhaize’s US chains remained offline, a week after the cyber incident forced the company to shut down some of its IT systems. Ahold Delhaize said it expected e-commerce services at its US brands to resume "in the coming days".
The US brands, which include Stop & Shop, Giant Food, Hannaford and Food Lion, collectively rank among the country’s largest food retailers. Deliveries at Belgian chain Delhaize resumed over the weekend.
Ahold Delhaize previously said that there was no evidence that any customer data had been stolen.
Physical stores of several chains have remained open, but have struggled with supplies as distribution channels were also affected.

items.title: Plaza cambiaria argentina se mantiene controlada con seguimiento de banco central
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El mercado cambiario argentino cerró con mermas el lunes mediante el habitual control del banco central (BCRA) que regula la liquidez cotidiana, en momentos en que el riesgo país saltaba a su máximo nivel en casi un año.
items.body:
El mercado cambiario argentino cerró con mermas el lunes mediante el habitual control del banco central (BCRA) que regula la liquidez cotidiana, en momentos en que el riesgo país saltaba a su máximo nivel en casi un año.
La autoridad monetaria aumentó en las últimas jornadas su accionar intervencionista, donde el viernes adquirió 68 millones de dólares y acumuló un saldo semanal positivo levemente superior a los 640 millones de dólares. En este inicio de semana, sumó 18 millones a sus reservas.
Las compras de la entidad elevaron las "reservas internacionales brutas a 50.236 millones de dólares y completando un saldo semanal comprador de 642 millones de dólares, el monto más alto registrado en los últimos tres meses", expresó Wise Capital.
"La estrategia oficial responde a la urgencia de abastecer de divisas al Tesoro de cara a los compromisos de deuda con tenedores de bonos Globales agendados para el próximo 9 de enero", añadió.
En este contexto, el peso mayorista se depreció un 0,43% a 1.524,5 unidades por dólar para la venta, con ligeras caídas en los precios de los contratos a futuro.
Por su parte, el riesgo país argentino trepaba a los 678 puntos básicos (2000 GMT), su mayor nivel desde finales de octubre del año pasado, con los bonos en el segmento extrabursátil cayendo un firme 1,3% por la misma debilidad de los negocios.
"La suba del riesgo país obedece a la incertidumbre global", aseguró el vocero presidencial Adrián Ravier en conferencia de prensa, con la certeza de que el país tiene instrumentos para afrontar presiones como más reservas e intercambio de monedas
con otros países, que "en caso de ser necesarios, se pueden usar".
La secretaría de Finanzas, dependiente del Ministerio de Economía, anunció una conversión de títulos que se llevará a cabo el martes.
"La operación permitirá a los tenedores del bono 'dollar-linked' con vencimiento a fines de octubre (D30O6) canjearlo por instrumentos con vencimiento a fines de noviembre, en enero de 2027 y en junio de 2027", afirmó la consultora Max Capital.
"Al igual que en anteriores vencimientos de instrumentos 'dollar-linked', el Tesoro ofrece un canje anticipado para reducir la potencial volatilidad cambiaria antes de la fijación del precio el 27 de octubre", añadió.
El índice accionario líder de Argentina, localmente conocido como Merval, pasó a llamarse desde este lunes MSCI Merval tras el acuerdo entre Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos (BYMA) y el proveedor global de índices MSCI.
"Como adelantamos al anunciar la alianza estratégica entre BYMA y MSCI (...) se lanzarán los nuevos índices de Renta Variable", dijo BYMA en un comunicado.
Y agregó que entre algunas de las principales características con la que contarán los índices será un valor inicial de 100.000 pesos para ambos y una moneda de publicación que será en pesos argentinos y dólares estadounidenses.
El flamante nuevo referencial MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) debutó con una caída del 1,84% al cierre dado el contexto desfavorable para los activos domésticos.
